text:
Marc Gatcomb is an undrafted forward from Woburn, Massachusetts, who worked his way through the AHL and the Islanders before landing in Vegas. His role is clear from one number: 72 hits in 20 games, at about 10.5 minutes a night.

The scoring is the problem. He has one goal and two points, and he has gone 17 straight games without a point on 3.7 expected goals. Unlike some droughts, this one isn't just bad luck. His chances have thinned out in recent games, and he is shooting 3.7% on 27 shots.

The five-on-five results are rough: Vegas has 35.3% of expected goals with him on the ice. His case rests on defense. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 91st percentile among forwards at keeping chances down in 2025-26, in under 500 minutes. The skating supports the forechecking role: his 32 bursts over 20 mph rank in the top quarter of the league. Watch whether his line can start tilting the ice, because hits alone won't keep a spot on a winning team.
headline: Gatcomb is hitting everything and scoring nothing
